title: Shh, This Is You Forever
subtitle: A memorial page that is far from being a proper memorial.

items.text: Shh, This Is You Forever
When does aging catch up with us?
Is it when we can no longer leap two steps at a time up the stairs? Or when the past is quietly forgotten and the number of white bottles in the cabinet keeps growing?
Or is it when time finally erodes the promise of our childhood dreams, and we are forced to leave them behind?

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Ms. Winnifred ... *cough, cough* ... don't you think my stubbornness is meaningless?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Not in the least, Mr. Brian.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Because you've found something that isn't eroded by time, haven't you?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: To this day, time hasn't changed your ideals. You still hold them tightly, unwilling to let go.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: I admire your conviction.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Hahaha ... *cough, cough* Hah!
The old man perks up as if he'd just been given a dose of adrenaline.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I suppose I'll achieve the ultimate victory soon, then ...

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: How wonderful, Ms. Winnifred.
Remembering something, he strains to lift his head again.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Then, will you still accept a copy of my film?
A soft sigh falls upon his ears.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: I'm sorry, I can't accept it.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Yes, I understand. It's not good enough. It's much too insignificant among your exquisite and unique collection.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: No, Mr. Brian, it's because it's too precious for me to endure its eventual loss.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: How long will this roll of film last—thirty, fifty years? Maybe a little longer?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: It's cruel to make someone so old see something so precious fade away. She has to watch as it's worn by time, witness its shape warp and curl.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Just as she has countless times before.
Brian smiles helplessly.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Yes, you're right. Now I can fully understand what you're saying. Besides, I can't run away in a huff like I did when I was young anymore.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: I have a gift for you, too.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Please don't, Ms. Winnifred.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I'm so old now. I can't repay you with anything of value. Are you trying to return that same pain to me?
Winnifred doesn't answer. Instead, she stands up and slowly approaches the bed.
The cool sea breeze seems to draw nearer.
A few drops of warm liquid fall on his face, like soft rain, or like a voice that has long been absent.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Mr. Brian, I remember those eyes from long ago. Green, timid, puerile ...

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: But also filled with immense courage and passion.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I ... I can see ...
Warmth rushes through every inch of his body, like an athlete finally returning to a familiar track.
Strength gradually returns to his body. He breathes deeply, his lungs filling with fresh air.
His vision clears, and the hands before him, still youthful and unscathed by bullet marks, clasp together in disbelief.
The sound of the tide becomes clearer in his ears.
It is the earnest echo of that time, more than sixty years ago.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Are they all alive?
The tables, chairs, and books swim in this boundless blue sea, tacitly dancing that same dance he saw all those years ago.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I remember this dance. They danced so well, so joyfully, that it made me forget all my pain.
His memories awaken.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Yes, this is it. This is the house from my dreams.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: *cough, cough* I've returned.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Ms. Winnifred, was it you? Have you given me this dream?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Mr. Brian, what a pleasure it is to see you again.
She reaches out her hand, as if greeting an old friend after many years.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: It's ... really you ...

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: It's always been you, hasn't it?
He reaches out a trembling hand, as if trying to touch that dream from his childhood.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Yes, it's me, my friend.
Time flows forward.
The water rises, then silently falls back to its origin.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Dr. David, please hurry. Dad's just in there.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: They open the door.

items.speaker: Illia
items.text: Dad ...

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: The room has returned to its original state, indistinguishable from when they left.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: The old man on the bed no longer stirs. His mouth is curved into a slight smile, as though he has drifted away into a sweet and peaceful dream.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: The notebook lies on his chest.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: No longer clutched in his hands, it has fallen open like a silent tombstone.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: A new page is presented. One bearing elegant handwriting in still-wet ink.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: "Thus, he lived a life fulfilled."

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: "He never owed anything to anyone, be they colleagues, lovers, children, or friends."

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: "And not for a single moment did he ever abandon his ideals."

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: "In memory of a brave old friend who steadfastly held to himself amid the raging rapids of time."
THE END
